description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a world-renowned Indian dish celebrated for its incredibly rich, creamy, and mildly spiced tomato-based gravy. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered to perfection in this luscious sauce, offering a delightful balance of sweet and savory flavors. It is a true culinary masterpiece that brings the warmth and comfort of Indian cuisine to your table.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in hot water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, 1 tsp garam masala, and 1/2 tsp salt. Mix well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours, to allow flavors to develop.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter or oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the finely chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and slit green chilies (if using), cooking for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, 1.5 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then add the drained soaked cashews and sugar. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil begins to separate from the sides.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Gravy
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the hot gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until it is completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky, restaurant-style texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan, using a spatula to press through all the liquid and discarding any remaining solids.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken pieces to the smooth gravy in the pan. Add the remaining 1 tsp garam masala, crushed kasoori methi, and salt to taste. Pour in the water or chicken broth and simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld beautifully and the chicken to absorb the rich sauce.

instructions.title: Add Cream and Garnish
instructions.text: Finally, stir in the heavy cream and heat gently without bringing it to a boil, as this can cause the cream to split. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro just before serving. Serve hot with naan, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For an even deeper color and flavor, marinate the chicken overnight. This allows the spices to penetrate fully, resulting in incredibly tender and succulent chicken.
Do not skip blending and straining the gravy. This step is crucial for achieving the characteristic velvety smooth texture of authentic Murgh Makhani, ensuring no onion or cashew bits remain.
Always add heavy cream at the very end and avoid boiling the gravy once it's incorporated, as this can cause the cream to split. Gently heat through for a rich, luxurious finish.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: A Timeless Indian Lunch Recipe

Few dishes capture the heart of Indian cuisine quite like Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, celebrated for its rich, creamy tomato gravy and tender pieces of chicken, has transcended borders to become a global favorite. While often enjoyed for dinner, its comforting flavors and relatively straightforward preparation make it an excellent choice for a hearty and satisfying Indian lunch recipe. Whether you’re cooking for a family meal or prepping a delicious lunch to enjoy throughout the week, Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani promises an explosion of flavors that are both luxurious and deeply comforting.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter," and that name perfectly encapsulates its essence. Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, this dish was famously created by Kundan Lal Gujral at Moti Mahal restaurant. The story goes that he combined leftover tandoori chicken with a rich tomato-based gravy, fortified with butter and cream, to create a dish that would become an instant classic.

At its core, Murgh Makhani features succulent pieces of chicken (traditionally tandoori-cooked, though home versions often pan-fry or bake it) swimming in a velvety sauce. This sauce is a masterful blend of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, a medley of aromatic spices, and generous amounts of butter and fresh cream, often finished with a touch of kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) for an unmistakable aroma. The result is a mildly spiced, subtly sweet, and incredibly rich curry that appeals to nearly every palate, making it a beloved staple in Indian restaurants and homes worldwide.

## Ingredients You Need for Butter Chicken

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients. Here's a breakdown of what you'll need:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
*   Plain yogurt
*   Ginger-garlic paste
*   Lemon juice
*   Red chili powder
*   Turmeric powder
*   Garam masala
*   Salt

For the Makhani (Butter) Gravy:
*   Unsalted butter
*   Onions, finely chopped or pureed
*   Ginger-garlic paste
*   Canned crushed tomatoes or fresh ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   Cashews (soaked in warm water for 30 minutes, then ground into a paste) – optional, for extra richness and thickness
*   Spices: Red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, ground coriander, cumin powder
*   Kasoori Methi (dried fenugreek leaves)
*   Sugar or honey (to balance the acidity of tomatoes)
*   Heavy cream or half-and-half
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth (to adjust consistency)

Garnish:
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped
*   A swirl of heavy cream

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Murgh Makhani

Making Murgh Makhani at home is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a truly delicious result:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** You have a few options here. For a traditional smoky flavor, you can broil the chicken in the oven until slightly charred and cooked through. Alternatively, heat a little oil in a pan and pan-fry the chicken pieces until golden brown and cooked. Set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt a generous amount of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped or pureed onions and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Build the Sauce:** Add the crushed tomatoes (or fresh tomato puree) to the pot. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have darkened slightly and the oil begins to separate. This step is crucial for deepening the flavor.

5.  **Add Spices and Cashews:** Stir in the red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, coriander, and cumin. Cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. If using, add the cashew paste and mix well. Cook for another 2-3 minutes.

6.  **Simmer and Blend:** Pour in about 1 cup of water or chicken broth, bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. For an incredibly smooth sauce, carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. Strain it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot for an even silkier texture (optional but recommended for restaurant-quality results).

7.  **Combine and Finish:** Return the blended sauce to the pot. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces, kasoori methi (crush it between your palms before adding to release its aroma), sugar or honey, and salt to taste. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the sauce's flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and a knob of fresh butter. Heat gently for a couple of minutes – do not boil after adding cream, as it can curdle.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken Results

Achieving truly exceptional Butter Chicken at home is within reach with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't rush the chicken marination. Longer marination times (up to 24 hours) lead to more tender and flavorful chicken that truly shines in the final dish.
*   **Quality Tomatoes Matter:** Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes or very ripe, flavorful fresh tomatoes. The tomatoes form the backbone of the sauce, so their quality significantly impacts the taste.
*   **Blend for Silkiness:** For that signature restaurant-style smooth sauce, blending the cooked gravy base until completely smooth, and then straining it, is a game-changer. It removes any fibrous bits from onions or tomatoes.
*   **Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream:** While you can adjust these for dietary preferences, the "butter" in Butter Chicken is non-negotiable for authentic flavor and richness. Add a final pat of butter and a swirl of cream just before serving for ultimate indulgence.
*   **Toasted Kasoori Methi:** Lightly toast the kasoori methi in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing and adding it. This intensifies its unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor.
*   **Low and Slow Simmer:** After adding the chicken to the sauce, allow it to simmer gently on low heat. This gives the chicken time to absorb the rich flavors of the Murgh Makhani gravy.

## Serving Suggestions for Indian Butter Chicken

Butter Chicken is incredibly versatile and pairs wonderfully with a variety of Indian breads and rice dishes, making it an ideal Indian lunch recipe.

*   **Naan Bread:** The classic pairing! Warm, soft naan is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan elevate the experience even further.
*   **Basmati Rice:** A mound of fluffy basmati rice, either plain or lightly spiced jeera (cumin) rice, provides a comforting contrast to the creamy curry.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** For a lighter option, whole wheat roti or flaky paratha also make excellent accompaniments.
*   **Side Salad or Raita:** A simple cucumber and onion salad or a cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) can cut through the richness of the Butter Chicken, offering a refreshing balance.
*   **Pickles and Chutneys:** A small dollop of your favorite Indian pickle or mango chutney can add an extra layer of flavor and zest.

## Variations and Substitutions for Murgh Makhani

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, you can easily adapt Murgh Makhani to suit different preferences or dietary needs:

*   **Healthier Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute some of the heavy cream with Greek yogurt (stirred in gently at the end to prevent curdling). You can also use a healthier oil for cooking the chicken.
*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Easily convert this into a vegetarian delight by replacing chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables. Paneer Makhani is a very popular dish on its own.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your liking. For a spicier kick, add a fresh green chili or a pinch of cayenne pepper. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have nut allergies, you can omit the cashews. The sauce will still be delicious, perhaps slightly thinner. A spoonful of gram flour (chickpea flour) roasted briefly in butter and then added to the sauce can help thicken it without nuts.
*   **Quick Version:** To save time, you can use pre-cooked rotisserie chicken or skip the marination step for the chicken (though flavor will be slightly less intense). You can also use good quality canned tomato sauce instead of pureeing fresh tomatoes.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a dish; it's a culinary experience. Its exquisite balance of flavors and textures makes it a perennial favorite. Whether you’re a seasoned cook or a beginner, trying your hand at this beloved Indian lunch recipe is a journey worth taking. Enjoy the process, and savor every rich, creamy bite!
